environment.cpu_model: AMD RYZEN AI MAX+ 395 w/ Radeon 8060S

suites.name: sqly and other SQL-over-CSV tools
suites.description: The same query on the same CSV file, from starting the process to its exit.

benchmarks.name: aggregate 100k
benchmarks.description: The top 10 countries by row count of the 100 000 customers in testdata/benchmark/customers100000.csv (12 columns, 17 MB), printed as CSV.

commands.name: sqly
commands.command: ${artifact} --output-format csv --sql "SELECT Country, COUNT(*) AS n FROM customers100000 GROUP BY Country ORDER BY n DESC, Country LIMIT 10" ${head_root}/../../testdata/benchmark/customers100000.csv

commands.name: trdsql
commands.command: trdsql -icsv -ih -oh "SELECT Country, COUNT(*) AS n FROM ${head_root}/../../testdata/benchmark/customers100000.csv GROUP BY Country ORDER BY n DESC, Country LIMIT 10"

commands.name: csvq
commands.command: csvq -r ${head_root}/../../testdata/benchmark -f csv "SELECT Country, COUNT(*) AS n FROM customers100000 GROUP BY Country ORDER BY n DESC, Country LIMIT 10"

commands.name: textql
commands.command: textql -header -output-header -sql "SELECT Country, COUNT(*) AS n FROM customers100000 GROUP BY Country ORDER BY n DESC, Country LIMIT 10" ${head_root}/../../testdata/benchmark/customers100000.csv

commands.name: duckdb
commands.command: duckdb -c "COPY (SELECT Country, COUNT(*) AS n FROM '${head_root}/../../testdata/benchmark/customers100000.csv' GROUP BY Country ORDER BY n DESC, Country LIMIT 10) TO '/dev/stdout' (HEADER)"

benchmarks.name: filter 100k
benchmarks.description: The e-mail address and city of every customer in Japan, sorted by address: a scan of all 100 000 rows that keeps 418 of them.

commands.name: sqly
commands.command: ${artifact} --output-format csv --sql "SELECT Email, City FROM customers100000 WHERE Country = 'Japan' ORDER BY Email" ${head_root}/../../testdata/benchmark/customers100000.csv

commands.name: trdsql
commands.command: trdsql -icsv -ih -oh "SELECT Email, City FROM ${head_root}/../../testdata/benchmark/customers100000.csv WHERE Country = 'Japan' ORDER BY Email"

commands.name: csvq
commands.command: csvq -r ${head_root}/../../testdata/benchmark -f csv "SELECT Email, City FROM customers100000 WHERE Country = 'Japan' ORDER BY Email"

commands.name: textql
commands.command: textql -header -output-header -sql "SELECT Email, City FROM customers100000 WHERE Country = 'Japan' ORDER BY Email" ${head_root}/../../testdata/benchmark/customers100000.csv

commands.name: duckdb
commands.command: duckdb -c "COPY (SELECT Email, City FROM '${head_root}/../../testdata/benchmark/customers100000.csv' WHERE Country = 'Japan' ORDER BY Email) TO '/dev/stdout' (HEADER)"

benchmarks.name: export 100k
benchmarks.description: Every row and column of the customers file written back out as CSV, so reading every value and writing every value is the whole cost. textql is left out: it reads the phone number 0389689232 as the number 389689232 and writes that, so its output differs from the other four.

benchmarks.name: aggregate 1m
benchmarks.description: The row count and the sum of one column of a generated CSV of 1 000 000 rows (4 columns, 38 MB), where loading the file is nearly the whole cost.

commands.name: sqly
commands.command: ${artifact} --output-format csv --sql "SELECT COUNT(*) AS n, SUM(id) AS total FROM bench" ${workdir}/bench.csv

commands.name: trdsql
commands.command: trdsql -icsv -ih -oh "SELECT COUNT(*) AS n, SUM(id) AS total FROM ${workdir}/bench.csv"

commands.name: csvq
commands.command: csvq -r ${workdir} -f csv "SELECT COUNT(*) AS n, SUM(id) AS total FROM bench"

commands.name: textql
commands.command: textql -header -output-header -sql "SELECT COUNT(*) AS n, SUM(id) AS total FROM bench" ${workdir}/bench.csv

commands.name: duckdb
commands.command: duckdb -c "COPY (SELECT COUNT(*) AS n, SUM(id) AS total FROM '${workdir}/bench.csv') TO '/dev/stdout' (HEADER)"
